title: What If It Rained Blood Red? In 2001 It Did, for Two Months

scenes.text: What if the rain came down blood red? In 2001, in southern India, it did.
It began on July 25th in Kerala and kept returning for two months. Some showers fell green, yellow, even black.
Each milliliter of the red water held about nine million tiny red particles.
Two physicists said they looked like cells with no DNA, and suggested they came from a comet.
Government botanists identified them instead: spores of a common alga called Trentepohlia.
DNA tests later agreed, with a twist. The closest match was a species known from Austria. The spores may have crossed continents inside clouds.

description:
What if it rained blood red? Between 25 July and 23 September 2001, red rain fell again and again on Kerala in southern India, with some showers reported as green, yellow or black. Each millilitre held about nine million red particles.
India's Centre for Earth Science Studies and the Tropical Botanic Garden found they were spores of the alga Trentepohlia, not the alien cells two physicists proposed. A 2015 DNA study identified the species as Trentepohlia annulata, previously reported only from Austria, and suggested the spores travelled in clouds over the ocean.
